title: Macbeth's Ambition
text:
Returning from victory in battle, the Scottish general Macbeth and his friend Banquo meet three witches. They hail Macbeth as the future king, and tell Banquo that his descendants will be kings. Macbeth writes to his wife, and Lady Macbeth, fearing he is too full of the milk of human kindness, pushes him to act. When King Duncan stays at their castle, Macbeth murders him in his sleep and takes the crown.

The first crime does not make him safe. It makes him afraid. Remembering the prophecy for Banquo, he hires murderers to kill his friend and his son Fleance. Banquo dies, but Fleance escapes, and at a banquet Macbeth sees Banquo's ghost in his own seat. When the thane Macduff flees to England, Macbeth has his wife and children slaughtered.

Scotland turns against him. Lady Macbeth, tormented, walks in her sleep trying to wash invisible blood from her hands, and dies. Macbeth, hollowed out, says that life is a tale told by an idiot, full of sound and fury, signifying nothing. The witches had promised that no man born of woman could harm him, but Macduff, who was cut from his mother's womb, meets him in battle and kills him. Duncan's son Malcolm becomes king.
lesson: A position won by wrongdoing has to be protected by more of it, and each step makes the next one easier. The safest moment to stop is before the first compromise.
people: Macbeth, Lady Macbeth, Banquo, Duncan, Macduff
